clue.text: Mutual respect's beginning with police car going off

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its opening letter, so only the first of respect's is used
going off suggests something that has gone wrong or exploded, so the letters of police car are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A police car speeding off as a gesture of shared regard between officers and public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' rearranges POLICE CAR into ECIPROCAL, which follows the R from 'respect's beginning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a mutual arrangement is one given and received equally by both parties.

clue.text: Loaded, but ridiculous

definitions.meaning: loaded is slang for having plenty of money, wealthy
ridiculous in the sense of an absurd claim, as in 'that's a bit much'

explanation.surface: Someone is wealthy, but the observer finds it absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: wealthy (loaded) and, colloquially, outrageous or laughable, as in 'that's a bit thick'.

clue.text: State of tension seeing coward struggling across line

indicators.note: one piece lies across another, spanning it, so the shuffled letters go round the next piece
something struggling is thrashing about, so the letters of coward are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A frightened person struggling to get over a line in a tense situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' turns COWARD into COD WAR, and 'across' sets it around L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cold War was the long period of hostility without open fighting between the Soviet bloc and the West.

clue.text: Maybe mum's got people with her controlling organisation

parts.note: a mum is an example of a parent; the 's is read as 'has'
people accompanying someone are her company

explanation.surface: A mother has got others around her and is running an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks mum as just one example of a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent company is a business that owns and controls subsidiary firms.

clue.text: Exotic oil on tap, available as choice

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, signalling the letters of oil on tap are put in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: An unusual oil offered on tap at a bar, should you want it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic' rearranges OIL ON TAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left to choice rather than required is not compulsory; a synonym phrase.

clue.text: A season up in the hills of Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to season food is to salt it

explanation.surface: A spell of time spent up in Africa's highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the word for season backwards; 'season' looks like a time of year but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlas Mountains are a range in north-west Africa, across Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.

clue.text: Stone circle left on peak, oddly

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of peak

explanation.surface: A stone circle left standing on a mountain top, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone circle' reads as one thing; Stone is the definition and circle gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemstone of silica with a milky, iridescent play of colour: an example of a precious stone.

clue.text: Parking on grass to get around parking twice, got ready

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece on another sits above it, coming first

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

indicators.note: one piece getting around another encircles it

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands

indicators.note: twice says the letter for parking is used two times over

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Instructions for parking on the verge, making a tight turn: someone getting set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the first P above the rest; 'to get around' wraps the grass round two more Ps, from 'twice'.
explanation.definitionFit: To prep is informal for to prepare, so its past form means made ready.

clue.text: Desperate attempt to survive holiday centre

parts.note: to last is to keep going, to survive
a resort is a place people go on holiday

explanation.surface: A frantic effort to keep a holiday camp in business.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the last thing one turns to when everything else has failed.

clue.text: Criminal pair one found in sect

indicators.note: found in says one piece is located inside another

parts.note: a cult is a sect
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Two people, one belonging to a religious group, turn out to be lawbreakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the guilty party, the wrongdoer responsible for an offence.

clue.text: Incapable of supporting oneself?

parts.note: read literally, a being without limbs to stand on; in British slang the word also means so drunk one cannot stand

explanation.surface: A question about someone unable to provide for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests financial dependence; it means having nothing to stand on, which British slang also uses for blind drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Without lower limbs one cannot stand up; British slang applies it to someone too drunk to stand.

clue.text: Doctors ring needing custom

parts.note: a ring is a group or gang of people
a custom is a usual practice

explanation.surface: Physicians call wanting more patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a telephone call; it is a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A group practice is several GPs (family doctors) working together, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: Viewer keen to see what's in store

definitions.text: Viewer keen to see what's in store

parts.words: Viewer keen to see what's in store
parts.note: 'in store' looks like the future; it means inside a shop, seen through its display glass

explanation.surface: Someone eager to learn what the future holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's in store' suggests fate; it is literally goods in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone browsing shop displays from the pavement without buying anything.

clue.text: Plots Conservative approach in the case of schools

indicators.note: in says the next pieces go inside the outer letters of schools
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
a line is an approach or policy, as in a party line

explanation.surface: Schemes about Tory policy on schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plots' looks like schemes or conspiracies; here it means narratives.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the plots of novels or films are their narrative threads.

clue.text: Go and cover for person switching sides

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
a coat is a covering layer, as of paint

explanation.surface: Someone told to go and cover for a deserter.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor or defector, one who abandons his party or cause for the opposing one.

clue.text: Digs suit

definitions.meaning: digs as a verb: spade-like tools used for digging, or the plural noun read as tools that dig
one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: Lodgings that are just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' is British slang for lodgings and 'suit' looks like a verb; both are nouns here, the tools and the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Digging tools in the plural, and the black card suit alongside clubs, hearts and diamonds.

clue.text: Look after property in strike about old customs

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to strike is to hit
customs are usages, ways things are done

explanation.surface: Caring for a building during a strike over traditional practices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the word for strike round the old customs; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind someone's home while they are away, living there to keep it safe.

clue.text: A person elected by vicar to refurbish

indicators.note: by means next to, so the vicar's piece stands beside the rest

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
an MP is a Member of Parliament, chosen by voters

explanation.surface: A politician chosen by the clergyman to redecorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a fresh look by renovating or overhauling something: a synonym.

clue.text: Governor's frailty, getting broody regularly

parts.note: a vice is a moral weakness or frailty

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of broody

explanation.surface: A ruler's weakness is becoming moody and brooding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Governor's' is read as 'Governor is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler governing a colony or province on behalf of a sovereign, as in British India.

clue.text: Criminal only disheartened with condition attached by judge initially

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of judge
with its heart taken out, only keeps just its outside letters

parts.note: a rider is a condition or clause added to a document

explanation.surface: A judge adds a condition when sentencing a criminal whose spirit is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steals a car to drive it recklessly for fun is a lawbreaker; noun use.

clue.text: Predicament laid out over English military award

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the shuffled letters enclose the next pieces
laid out suggests spread about, so the letters of laid are set in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
MM is the Military Medal, a British gallantry award

explanation.surface: A dilemma set out over an English soldier's decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LAID to DILA, which goes 'over' E and MM, the Military Medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation where every choice is unwelcome is a difficult plight: synonym.

clue.text: Limp and miss a platform — I must go to California shortly

parts.note: to lack something is to miss it, be without it
a dais is a raised platform
Cal is a short form of California

explanation.surface: Someone limping and missing a stage must head off to California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limp' looks like a verb about walking; it is an adjective, meaning lacking energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking vigour or enthusiasm, listless and half-hearted: a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Incus discovered in Roman villa

indicators.note: discovered in says the letters are found buried within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A small bone excavated at an ancient Roman house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' adds flavour: incus is the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: The incus is the anvil-shaped middle-ear bone, its Latin name meaning the blacksmith's block.

clue.text: Couple lacking source of cash for bank of Scotland

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the word for couple

parts.note: a brace is a pair, a couple

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Two people short of money turn to the Bank of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank of Scotland' looks like the bank's name; it is a Scottish hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots dialect for a hillside or steep slope beside a river: a regional word.

clue.text: Hurry back and watch Kirov's last dancer

indicators.note: back means the word for hurry is read in reverse

parts.note: to hurry is to run
to eye something is to watch it

indicators.note: last means the final letter of Kirov's

explanation.surface: Rush back and see the final dancer of the Kirov Ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kirov is the St Petersburg ballet company, where this dancer trained.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev, the Soviet-born ballet star who defected to the West in 1961, is an example.

clue.text: Gently boil outside with fish, for example

indicators.note: outside means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to simmer is to cook just below boiling

explanation.surface: Poaching some fish gently in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' looks like the food; it is a creature that moves through water.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish are an example of creatures that move through water by propelling themselves.

clue.text: A measure of whisky enjoyed in Scottish island

indicators.note: A measure of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dram of Scotch drunk on a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'in', but 'in' is a link word joining wordplay to definition; the island alone is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Very popular, and completely sane, drinking a gallon

parts.note: all means wholly, completely

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: to be all there is to be sane, so there alone stands for sane

explanation.surface: Fashionable and fully rational, despite downing a gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all there' is an idiom for mentally sound, but only its second word stands for sane here; 'drinking' takes in A and G.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being the current fashion, widely popular for the time being.
